parts.text: Which claim correctly explains how sexual reproduction mixes information without doubling instructions each generation?

options.text: Each gamete carries half the genetic material; joining them makes a complete mix from two parents without doubling every generation.
Each gamete carries a full set, so joining doubles the instructions every generation.
Mixing comes from only one parent, so brothers and sisters must look identical.
Fertilisation avoids mixing; offspring match only one parent.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Parul learns that in sexual reproduction each gamete carries half of a parent's genetic material before male and female gametes join.

part_answers.answer: Half-material gametes prevent doubling; fertilisation still mixes information from two parents.

teacher.key_rationale: Gametes carry half the genetic material so fertilisation mixes two parents without doubling instructions each generation. Full-set doubling, one-parent-only mixing, or no mixing all miss that hinge.
